note: criterion (d)'s flip-count bound, computed from the committed stage artefacts. The unit is the smallest observation the producing stage records and the bound is the FEWEST unit inversions that could reverse the number's verdict (inversions applied strongest-support-first). A verdict that asserts an ABSENCE has no inversion bound: it is reversed by MORE support, so its margin is reported as a distance to the decision boundary instead. `kind` marks exact bounds apart from estimates under a stated assumption.

F1_1_witness.unit: block (a problem x profile cell; 39 of them, each block's median taken over its own 16 paired observations)
F1_1_witness.asserts: an effect (the sign channel is resolvable)

count.rule: a MAJORITY of blocks (20 of 39) have |loss gap| above their own cluster MDE

interval.rule: the 95% interval over the 39 block medians excludes 0

F1_1_witness.paired_observations_rule: a median over 16 paired observations is inverted only if more than half of them move
F1_1_witness.note: the IDENTITY leg of this claim (the scalar-feature gap is exactly 0 in every block) has no flip bound: no change to the streams can move a quantity that is 0 by construction, and that is the stronger statement

ski.unit: cluster (208 per row; the stage records the cluster mean and its interval only)
ski.asserts: an ABSENCE (this problem is not resolved)
ski.rule: the row's 95% cluster interval excludes 0 AND the advantage exceeds 2 cluster MDEs (the registered reading of a resolvable contrast)
ski.distance_rule: the observed ratio sits this many cluster MDEs BELOW the 2-MDE bar; only MORE support moves it across, so no inversion bound exists for this verdict
ski.kind: exact distance (from the recorded ratio), no inversion bound

sched.unit: cluster (208 per row; the stage records the cluster mean and its interval only)
sched.rule: the row's 95% cluster interval excludes 0 AND the advantage exceeds 2 cluster MDEs (the registered reading of a resolvable contrast)
sched.kind: ESTIMATE -- the stage records the cluster mean and interval, not the cluster values, so the mean-shift is assumed to come from equal-magnitude inversions

paging.unit: comparable pair of profiles (72 pairs over 13 profiles; ties dropped)
paging.rule: Kendall tau of mean gain against the tail read as higher-is-better is > 0
paging.kind: exact (every pair is recomputed from the recorded rows)

paging.unit: not derivable: the stage records one aggregate per problem

paging.rule: the advantage over MDE under the EVEN synthetic target is negative
paging.distance_rule: the aggregate sits this many MDEs below zero
paging.kind: the margin is exact; NO bound in units is derivable, because the per-unit rows behind the aggregate are not recorded -- stated as such rather than estimated into a number
